title: Hiring the Executive Team (VPs and C-Suite)

parts.visual:
A startup reaches 100 employees. The CEO is overwhelmed. They decide to hire a VP of Sales. The CEO interviews a candidate who used to run sales at a massive, slow, 10,000-person corporation. The CEO hires them. Three months later, sales drop to zero.

The Hiring Trap:
1. Big Company Bias: Startups often mistakenly hire executives from massive corporations like IBM or Oracle, assuming they are geniuses. But big company executives rely on massive budgets and established brands.
2. The Builder Executive: A startup needs executives who have experience specifically scaling a company from $10M to $50M. They must know how to build the machine from scratch, not just operate an existing one.
parts.audio: Hiring an executive is the highest-leverage decision a CEO makes. If you hire the right VP, your company doubles in size. If you hire the wrong VP, they will hire 20 mediocre people beneath them, and you will spend a year trying to fix the damage.

questions.question: A CEO is interviewing a VP of Marketing. The candidate says, 'My first step is to hire a $500,000 PR agency to build our brand.' What should the CEO do?
options: Do not hire them. They are an 'Operator', not a 'Builder'. A startup needs a VP who will open their laptop, write the ad copy themselves, and growth-hack the first 10,000 users before they ask for a massive agency budget.
questions.correct_answer: Do not hire them. They are an 'Operator', not a 'Builder'. A startup needs a VP who will open their laptop, write the ad copy themselves, and growth-hack the first 10,000 users before they ask for a massive agency budget.
questions.explanation: Startups need leaders who are willing to get their hands dirty.

questions.question: Listen to the famous hiring rule from Silicon Valley. What must the new executive be?
questions.tts_text: If you are the CEO, and you are hiring a VP of Engineering, that VP must be vastly superior to you at engineering. If they are not intimidatingly smart in their domain, you are hiring a subordinate, not an executive.
options: The 'Smarter Than You' Rule. The entire point of the C-Suite is to cover the CEO's weaknesses. You hire a CFO because they understand financial models you cannot comprehend. You must hire people who push back on your bad ideas.
questions.correct_answer: The 'Smarter Than You' Rule. The entire point of the C-Suite is to cover the CEO's weaknesses. You hire a CFO because they understand financial models you cannot comprehend. You must hire people who push back on your bad ideas.
questions.explanation: A CEO who hires weak executives is driven by ego, not strategy.

questions.question: What is 'Title Inflation' in early-stage startups?
options: Making the font bigger on business cards.

Giving a 22-year-old junior employee the title 'Chief Marketing Officer' just because they were the first marketing hire. Two years later, when the company needs a real, experienced CMO, you have to fire or demote the 22-year-old, causing massive drama.
questions.correct_answer: Giving a 22-year-old junior employee the title 'Chief Marketing Officer' just because they were the first marketing hire. Two years later, when the company needs a real, experienced CMO, you have to fire or demote the 22-year-old, causing massive drama.

questions.question: Why do VCs often force founders to use professional 'Executive Search Firms' (Headhunters) for C-Suite roles?
options: Access to passive talent. The best VP of Engineering in the world is not currently looking for a job; they are already highly paid and busy. A search firm has the network to quietly approach them and convince them to jump to your startup.
questions.correct_answer: Access to passive talent. The best VP of Engineering in the world is not currently looking for a job; they are already highly paid and busy. A search firm has the network to quietly approach them and convince them to jump to your startup.
